text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They learn patterns in language, which lets them predict the next word in a sentence. When you give them a prompt—a question or instruction—they generate a response based on those patterns. This is called prompt engineering, where the way you phrase your request greatly affects the quality of the answer. LLMs can write essays, summarize information, and even code, but they have limits. They don't truly understand meaning; they can make up facts, and their knowledge stops at their training date. So, while powerful, they require careful use.
